# **Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member Onboarding** – nothing bridges signup to first class to retention (highest churn risk window)
- **Cancellation & Churn** – no documented win-back, pause protocol, or exit interview process
- **Member Checkins** – no scheduled touchpoint SOP (30/60/90 day, post-class, low-activity alerts)
- **Data Privacy & GDPR** – legal/compliance blind spot; no retention, consent, or breach protocol
- **Referral Programme** – no mechanics, incentive tracking, or member comms for referral lifecycle
- **Order Supplies & Sundries** – reorder triggers, vendor contacts, stock levels undefined
- **Coaching Development Roadmap** – no progression path, skills audit, or upskilling schedule for coaches
- **Class Quality Audit Checklist** – no standardised observation tool for coaching consistency or member experience
- **Transformation Pillars** – no framework linking member outcomes to studio narrative (used in marketing/retention)

---

# **Needs updating**

- **Coaches SOPs (19/22)** – likely missing: Weekly Key Coach Tasks, session setup/breakdown standards, difficult-member scripts, substitute/absence protocol
- **Facilities (7/8)** – presumed gap: equipment maintenance schedule, emergency protocols, cleaning checklists post-class
- **Marketing (5/5)** – check if retention-loop comms (welcome series, milestone congratulations, re-engagement campaigns) are baked in or marketing-only
- **Clients area (26/36)** – audit which 10 are missing; suspect: milestone celebration, pause workflow, member outcomes tracking

# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

**Immediate action (today):**
- Call 3-5 of your best-performing coaches individually. Ask: "What do members ask you most about pricing? What confuses them?" Document exact phrases. Use these in your menu language—it'll resonate because it addresses real friction points.

**Structure it for TWO audiences simultaneously:**
- **Coach menu**: List every service tier with *exact* what-you-deliver specs (e.g., "Small Group (4-6 max, 45 min, 1:1 form check per person)" not just "Small Group Coaching"). Coaches need to know boundaries so they stop over-delivering or under-delivering.
- **Member menu**: Strip out internal jargon. Use outcome language instead ("Build strength + confidence" beats "Progressive resistance training"). Include what's bundled vs. à la carte—members hate surprise add-ons.

**Price architecture hack:**
- Anchor your premium offering first, then show "lite" versions below it. Psychology: members will trade down consciously rather than all anchor to your cheapest option. Test pricing on your 5 most-engaged members before publishing.

**Distribution format:**
- One-page PDF (print it—laminate copies for the gym floor). Pin to your website under a stupidly obvious button. Every new inquiry should receive this within 2 hours, auto-sent. This kills the "let me think about pricing" limbo.

**The real output:** You're not just listing services—you're eliminating decision paralysis for both coaches and prospects. That's where growth happens.
